findings.pdf_says: (argument-2₁ / (1 + argument-1) + argument-2₂ / (1 + argument-1) ** 2) ... (argument-2₁ / (1 + argument-1) ** 1) ... (argument-2ₙ / (1 + argument-1) ** n))) where argument-1 and argument-2ᵢ in the terms of the SUM function (subscripts 1, 2, n and i printed below the line)
findings.markdown_says: (argument-21 / (1 + argument-1) + argument-22 / (1 + argument-1) \*\* 2) ... (argument-21 / (1 + argument-1) \*\* 1) ... (argument-2n / (1 + argument-1) \*\* n))) ... where argument-1 and argument-2i in the terms of the SUM function
findings.why_it_matters: 15.69.3 PRESENT-VALUE returned values: the subscripts that index the occurrences of argument-2 are flattened onto the baseline, so the equivalent expressions read as references to differently named operands 'argument-21', 'argument-22', 'argument-2n', 'argument-2i' instead of the 1st, 2nd, nth and ith occurrence of argument-2.
